scope: The share price as a weapon and its risk: stock-funded acquisitions and licence-and-hire deals 2006-2026, buybacks and stock pay, loss-funded bets, the talent raid, and the busts that ended the strategy.

facts.notes: Paid in cash and stock; Instagram had about 13 employees (not verified here).

flashpoints.title: Stock buys the rival before it grows
flashpoints.advantage: a rising share price as currency
flashpoints.mechanism: Facebook paid about $1bn in cash and stock for a photo app before it could become a rival network.
flashpoints.outcome: Instagram, bought at $1bn, joined Meta; WhatsApp followed in 2014 at $19.3bn, 79% paid in stock and restricted stock.

flashpoints.title: $15bn of shares for a messenger
flashpoints.mechanism: $12bn in Facebook shares plus $3bn of restricted stock units, retaining WhatsApp staff, bought the most popular messenger out of the market.
flashpoints.outcome: A $19.3bn price, largest deal to date; the messenger now has billions of users inside Meta.

flashpoints.title: Licence-and-hire: buying talent without buying the company
flashpoints.advantage: cash pile and share price to outbid for founders
flashpoints.mechanism: Google paid about $2.7bn for Character.AI talent and $2.4bn for Windsurf leaders, taking them after OpenAI's $3bn bid fell apart.
flashpoints.outcome: The startups remained legally independent, so the deals avoided a merger review; Microsoft had used the same structure for Inflection at $650m.

flashpoints.title: Meta pays for a lab
flashpoints.advantage: share price funds pay no start-up can match
flashpoints.mechanism: Meta bought a stake in Scale AI for $14.3bn, hired its CEO, and offered researchers packages up to $300m over four years.
flashpoints.outcome: Altman said none of OpenAI's best accepted; at least ten offers went to OpenAI staff. Meta's pay in stock rests on its own share price.

flashpoints.title: The market punishes the loss-funded bet
flashpoints.advantage: ad profits funding a VR land grab
flashpoints.mechanism: Reality Labs lost billions a year, funded by the ad business; when profit declined the share price fell 27%.
flashpoints.outcome: About $230bn of value gone in a day; Reality Labs has lost $80bn since 2020 and Meta still expects $18-19bn of loss in 2026.

flashpoints.title: The biggest company in the world, then 431bn lost
flashpoints.advantage: a stock price high enough to buy a whole sector
flashpoints.mechanism: At the dot-com peak Cisco was worth over $500bn and paid for acquisitions with richly priced shares.
flashpoints.outcome: The bubble burst: $431bn of value lost; the Nasdaq fell 78% by October 2002.

flashpoints.title: 47bn of valuation, then bankruptcy
flashpoints.mechanism: WeWork raised $12.8bn at valuations up to $47bn and grew faster than its leases could earn.
flashpoints.outcome: The IPO was cancelled in 2019; it listed by SPAC in 2021 and filed for Chapter 11 on 6 November 2023, with SoftBank affiliates taking 20% of the reorganised firm.

flashpoints.title: Shares fold a loss-making lab into a profitable rocket firm
flashpoints.advantage: an all-stock merger at a 1.25 trillion valuation
flashpoints.mechanism: SpaceX swapped its own shares for xAI at a negotiated mark, tying the lab's compute needs to the parent's balance sheet and a coming IPO.
flashpoints.outcome: A combined entity valued at about $1.25 trillion; SpaceX listed in June 2026 at $135 a share.

flashpoints.title: Losses funded by a valuation
flashpoints.advantage: investor belief funds a burn that exceeds revenue
flashpoints.mechanism: OpenAI burned $3.7bn in Q1 2026 on $5.7bn of revenue and forecasts $278bn of cash burn to 2030, all funded by investors and partners who trade capital for compute demand.
flashpoints.outcome: The strategy works while capital stays cheap; if funding stops the burn cannot be sustained, which is how WeWork and FTX ended.

flashpoints.title: NVIDIA takes out an inference rival
flashpoints.advantage: a cash pile that can buy a competitor's leaders
flashpoints.mechanism: NVIDIA licensed Groq's technology and took its founder and engineers; CNBC put the deal at $20bn in cash, three times Groq's last valuation of $6.9bn.
flashpoints.outcome: Groq stays nominally independent; the rival's team now works for the incumbent. The $20bn figure is reported, not confirmed.

notes: Unverified or excluded: Amazon Leo revenue; below-cost pricing is not proved by a primary source (only a Jefferies price-war finding). The $2.7bn Character.AI figure is WSJ-sourced and not confirmed by Google. NVIDIA-Groq $20bn is CNBC-reported. Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA 8-Ks on sec.gov refused script fetches (403); company IR pages used where they fetched.
